newsitem.title: USA: IMM currency futures trade mixed in light activity.
newsitem.headline: IMM currency futures trade mixed in light activity.

text.p: IMM currency futures were mixed in light trade, as yen fell towards support and marks expanded opening gains.
"Marks are flattening like they're trying to base," one technical analyst said. "But the trend remains down."
He said June marks would have to rise above $0.6055 before reversing its long-term trend, which has been in place since September 1996.
However, June marks were unable to rise above the pivot point of $0.5935 after the German Ifo economics institute said the business climate in west Germany improved in April.
Ifo's climate index rose to 94.7 from 92.6 and was at the high end of expectations.
Bundesbank council member Olaf Sievert said growth in German money supply was also stronger than expected, with April growth at 6.7 percent.
However, Sievert said he saw no need to change German interest rates, and that inflation prospects for the current year were favorable.
On Wednesday's GLOBEX session, June marks rose to $0.5993, holding below the 1-1/2-week high of $0.6005.
The divergence between June marks and June yen futures was reflected in the mark/yen cash cross rate, which rebounded overnight.

June yen's long-trend, however, turned higher when it spiked above $0.008335 on May 9, he said. Overnight comments from Tadashi Ogawa, vice finance minister of Japan's Ministry of Finance, supported the dollar/yen's rise above 115.00.
Ogawa said he agreed with the Bank of Japan's (BOJ) low interest rate policy.
June yen nudged towards support at $0.008647, which currently corresponds to a dollar/yen spot level of 116.00.
Further support is at $0.008625, or about 116.30 spot, and at $0.008599, or about 116.65 spot.
While the long-term trend remains bearish for marks, the trend for Swiss francs has turned bullish, he said.
He said the long-term trend for June Swiss francs turned bullish when the contract rose above $0.7059 on May 9. June set a 4-1/2-month high of $0.7281 on Wednesday's GLOBEX session.
Meanwhile, June sterling dipped to $1.6366, with the pivot point at $0.6312, the 100-day moving average. However, the currency remains stuck in a sideways range.
Canadian dollar futures were also lower, while June Mexican pesos set a contract high of $0.126100 at the opening.

At 0902 CDT/1402 GMT, June yen was off $0.000112 at $0.008675, marks were up $0.0023 at $0.5932, Swiss francs were $0.0004 higher at $0.7123, sterling fell $0.0062 at $1.6362, Canadian dollars were off $0.0014 at $0.7314, Australian dollars were down $0.0047 at $0.7822.
